basis: Sightline 1.3.0 RC10 preview, documentation revision 26, 11 November 2026

rows.name: Product type
rows.options: Desktop teleprompter with a translucent script overlay, voice control and production metadata.
rows.limits: A separate recording application or camera supplies the production video.

rows.name: Price and account
rows.options: Sightline Prompter is free to download and use, with no required Sightline account or subscription.
rows.limits: Optional third-party services can have their own charges and accounts.

rows.name: App source and licence
rows.options: Public GitHub source under the MIT licence; adapted from Electron Teleprompter.
rows.limits: Preserve applicable copyright and licence notices when redistributing.

rows.name: Desktop platforms
rows.options: Windows, macOS Apple silicon and Intel, and Linux distribution targets.
rows.limits: Physical hardware validation varies by platform; macOS hardware and VoiceOver checks remain outstanding.

rows.name: Local desktop operation
rows.options: Ordinary reading, editing and steady prompting run on the computer.
rows.limits: First downloads, updates, linked documents and online services require connectivity.

rows.name: Packaged installation
rows.options: Downloadable desktop packages; Windows installer and app branding.
rows.limits: Signing and operating-system security prompts are described in the installation guide.

rows.name: Windows process identity
rows.options: Short Sightline Prompter name in packaged Windows metadata.
rows.limits: Existing installed releases need an updated build to change their process description.

rows.name: Optional components
rows.options: Component checks and setup for the offline speech model, AI agent kit and external integrations.
rows.limits: Detecting a component does not validate its hardware, permissions or complete configuration.

rows.name: Missing dependency feedback
rows.options: Dependent controls explain missing components and offer the relevant setup route.
rows.limits: Available functions still depend on connection and permission state.

rows.name: Update and compatibility checks
rows.options: Version information and app/plugin compatibility feedback.
rows.limits: A detected version is not automatic installation or a passed acceptance test.

rows.name: Mode selection
rows.options: One Notes/page, Voice or Scroll choice in Mode and pace; relevant controls follow the selected mode.
rows.limits: Switching modes retains response, pace and countdown values; Voice requires enabled speech and microphone input.

rows.name: Steady scrolling
rows.options: Automatic scrolling at a chosen words-per-minute pace.
rows.limits: Timings are estimates and depend on the script and delivery.

rows.name: Voice following
rows.options: Advances through the script as recognised speech matches the words being read.
rows.limits: Requires microphone access and a configured local or online speech engine.

rows.name: Page and talking-point mode
rows.options: Notes mode displays pages of talking points; headings or explicit page breaks divide them.
rows.limits: Pages advance through navigation controls rather than continuous speech alignment.

rows.name: Start, pause and resume
rows.options: Toolbar, keyboard, voice and enabled remote controls.
rows.limits: Recorder behaviour is separately configured in the OBS section.

rows.name: Current-section status
rows.options: Yellow section/total pill on the persistent recorder status row.
rows.limits: Explicitly paged Notes shows page/total. Follows script navigation and retakes, including when the toolbar hides.

rows.name: On air reading view
rows.options: A separate On air state changes the operator/reading presentation and configured backing.
rows.limits: On air describes the prompter view; use the confirmed recording pill to check the recorder.

rows.name: Restart and return to top
rows.options: Return to the beginning; reset can also restore normal pace and clear the pacing clock.
rows.limits: Returning to top and starting a fresh timed run are distinct actions.

rows.name: Section navigation
rows.options: Previous, next and numbered section jumps; section retakes. RC5 adds an optional Voice-only Start from section heading preference for a spoken lead-in.
rows.limits: Off by default; first body line remains the default. Headings retain their section identity for editorial trimming; no automatic verified cut boundary.

rows.name: Speed and responsiveness
rows.options: Change steady WPM or Scroll catch-up speed during use; 100% is normal.
rows.limits: Catch-up speed affects display movement, not recognition. RC9 accepts ordered nearby common phrases; RC10 confines unordered automatic matching to the current section. Explicit Resync can search the whole script.

rows.name: Start countdown
rows.options: Set a countdown before Scroll mode starts moving.
rows.limits: Does not delay Voice or Notes/page mode, and does not itself start an external recorder.

rows.name: Section targets
rows.options: Per-section WPM and target duration, plus script-wide pacing instructions.
rows.limits: Targets guide delivery; they do not guarantee the final running time.

rows.name: Pace feedback
rows.options: Pacing light, elapsed time, progress and estimated time remaining.
rows.limits: Speech-derived figures require useful recognition data.

rows.name: Sentence and reading position
rows.options: Reading-line marker, sentence highlight and focus band.
rows.limits: These are reading aids rather than a measure of eye contact.

rows.name: First spoken line at start
rows.options: Long preparation notes hide for delivery. Position the first body line, or optionally the section heading in RC5 Voice mode.
rows.limits: Use production comments for setup. The Voice-only heading preference is retained but unused in Scroll/Notes.

rows.name: Offline speech recognition
rows.options: On-computer recognition with a downloadable local model.
rows.limits: Initial component download and microphone permission are required; results depend on voice and environment.

rows.name: Recognition language
rows.options: The supplied offline Zipformer model and current recognition configuration use English.
rows.limits: Do not assume multilingual recognition because the external provider offers other languages.

rows.name: Online speech recognition
rows.options: Optional Deepgram engine with the user's API key.
rows.limits: Requires internet access, a Deepgram account and its service terms; audio leaves the computer.

rows.name: Microphone choice
rows.options: Select the input used for voice following and command recognition.
rows.limits: Device availability, drivers and operating-system permissions apply.

rows.name: Listening modes
rows.options: In voice mode, Always listening, or Off.
rows.limits: Always listening keeps microphone recognition active while prompting is stopped.

rows.name: Wake word
rows.options: Prompter, Computer, Teleprompter or Director.
rows.limits: Wake-word recognition is speech recognition, not guaranteed keyword detection.

rows.name: Reading and display commands
rows.options: Go, pause, slower, faster, bigger, smaller, back, next and return to top.
rows.limits: Enable command listening; several phrases have documented aliases.

rows.name: Retake and edit commands
rows.options: Again, marker, back to marker, keeper and scrap that; bookmark flags are no longer drawn.
rows.limits: Ratings and markers describe the take log; they do not cut video automatically.

rows.name: Spoken section selection
rows.options: Select numbered sections, including natural spoken numbers.
rows.limits: A section number can act as a spoken slate and a retake instruction.

rows.name: Explicit recording commands
rows.options: RC8: record, start recording, begin and record take confirm OBS before delivery; finish recording, and record on, off, pause or resume remain.
rows.limits: OBS integration and recording-control permission must be enabled. Go, practice and start practice run the prompter with OBS unchanged.

rows.name: Head-guide voice commands
rows.options: Guide on and guide off request a definite visible or hidden state.
rows.limits: Controls the manual guide; it does not detect a face.

rows.name: Voice recovery and resync
rows.options: Listener health/recovery events and a resync command to find the reading position.
rows.limits: Noise, silence, paraphrasing and lost recognition can still require intervention.

rows.name: Recognition corrections
rows.options: Personal word corrections and sound-alike handling for script alignment.
rows.limits: Corrections do not retrain the speech engine or guarantee command recognition.

rows.name: Heard report and tracing
rows.options: Inspect recognised words for troubleshooting; separate optional command-word tracing.
rows.limits: Tracing can capture nearby conversation while listening; it is off by default.

rows.name: Command help
rows.options: Grouped What can I say window and contextual help.
rows.limits: Recording commands are shown only when the relevant OBS controls are enabled.

rows.name: Markdown and plain text
rows.options: Open `.md`, `.markdown` and `.txt` scripts.
rows.limits: Markdown structure provides the richest control over sections and directions.

rows.name: Word and rich text
rows.options: Import `.docx` and `.rtf` documents.
rows.limits: Conversion creates a reading script; it is not a full word-processing layout editor.

rows.name: PDF import
rows.options: Extract readable text from PDF files.
rows.limits: Image-only scans need OCR elsewhere; complex columns and layouts can require cleanup.

rows.name: HTML import
rows.options: Open `.html` and `.htm` script files.
rows.limits: Imported content is for prompting, not a complete browser application.

rows.name: Google Docs links
rows.options: Import accessible Google Docs content.
rows.limits: Sharing and internet access must permit retrieval; private account access is not implied.

rows.name: Built-in Markdown editor
rows.options: CodeMirror editor, preview toggle, save, Save as and unsaved-change prompts.
rows.limits: The app does not replace a full collaborative document suite.

rows.name: External editing
rows.options: Watch an opened file and refresh when it changes externally.
rows.limits: Watching pauses during built-in editing to avoid conflicting edits.

rows.name: Script slots
rows.options: Nine quick-access slots, recent files and switching controls.
rows.limits: A slot points to its script; clearing a slot is separately confirmed.

rows.name: Slot clearing protection
rows.options: Confirmation before clearing an occupied slot.
rows.limits: Keep source files backed up independently of slot assignments.

rows.name: Sample scripts
rows.options: Twelve shipped samples; Start here is a twelve-stop core/RC feature tour. Focused voice, framing, recording, Notes and handover demos use separate setup comments and short cues.
rows.limits: Protected originals: save a copy to edit. Recording actions are opt-in exercises. The formatting diagnostic intentionally contains one unknown tag. See [Demo guide](DEMO-SCRIPTS.md).

rows.name: Recording preview sample
rows.options: Preparation, Continuous and linked recording, explicit commands and handover walkthrough.
rows.limits: Exercise recorder controls only with the intended test setup connected.

rows.name: Exact recording script
rows.options: Preserve the source actually used, including section IDs, slide cues and directions, in the edit pack.
rows.limits: The export is the recording snapshot, which can differ from a later file edit.

rows.name: Ordinary scripts
rows.options: Read a script without adding compulsory application directives.
rows.limits: Optional directions add workflow control when needed.

rows.name: Sections and IDs
rows.options: Structured headings organise navigation, takes, targets and handover.
rows.limits: Stable section identity helps an editor match the recording script.

rows.name: Short delivery cues
rows.options: Square-bracket notes such as `[smile]`, `[think]` or `[point]` remain available inline.
rows.limits: Unquoted direction words are excluded from spoken word counts and alignment.

rows.name: Pointing and graphic intent
rows.options: RC3 preview: `[point left: graphic-label]`, right/up/down, diagonals and centre. Uses existing inline appearance controls; optional labels remain silent even in quotes.
rows.limits: Directions mean the presenter's own sides. Section-body cues are captured with the script and take; the editor verifies gesture and recorded orientation. No automatic asset insertion or gesture detection.

rows.name: Quoted spoken cues
rows.options: `[Say: "Section one"]` distinguishes words intended to be spoken.
rows.limits: Quoted words are included in the spoken script; do not use this form for silent instructions.

rows.name: Long production comments
rows.options: HTML comments hold preparation instructions; visible while paused and hidden during delivery. RC6 leaves opening comments clear of floating session controls, including wrapped rows.
rows.limits: All comment contents, including quoted words and directive examples, are excluded from speech tracking and command execution.

rows.name: Direction display
rows.options: Normal, dimmed or hidden bracket directions; quoted spoken words remain visible.
rows.limits: RC3 pointing labels stay silent, including quotes. Long production comments follow the separate paused/delivering rule.

rows.name: Manual script stops
rows.options: Scroll honours `{stop}`. RC10 Voice positions the next spoken passage and continues listening; Retake remains on the completed section until next delivery.
rows.limits: Explicit spoken Pause, off-script holds and sound checks retain deliberate controls. Finish recording explicitly.

rows.name: Timed pauses
rows.options: `{pause: 3s}` provides a countdown in Scroll mode.
rows.limits: Voice treats the timed tag as a visible beat cue; it does not hold, count down or pause linked recording.

rows.name: Named markers
rows.options: `{marker}` or `{marker: Setup}` creates a navigation and edit reference.
rows.limits: Navigation/log anchors remain without on-screen bookmark flags. Timing references are not verified frame-accurate cuts.

rows.name: Off-script passages
rows.options: `{listen: off}` and `{listen: on}` hold following and voice commands during ad-libs; manual continuation is required.
rows.limits: Enabled scratch audio and production recording can continue independently; this is not a whole-microphone privacy switch.

rows.name: Script sound checks
rows.options: `{soundcheck: room}` and `{soundcheck: voice}` request the appropriate check.
rows.limits: Measurement uses the selected input and the current acoustic conditions.

rows.name: Script control commands
rows.options: `{prompter: ...}` supports documented display, pace and marker actions.
rows.limits: Only documented commands are supported.

rows.name: Script recording commands
rows.options: Optional `{record: on}`, `{record: off}`, `{record: pause}` and `{record: resume}`.
rows.limits: Require enabled OBS recording controls; loading a script never executes them.

rows.name: Pace, notes and page directives
rows.options: Section WPM/targets, script pacing, `{mode: notes}` and `{page}`.
rows.limits: The script checker documents supported values and catches unknown directives.

rows.name: Floating HUD cues
rows.options: RC4: a gold short-cue pill during delivery; paused Review restores inline bracket directions.
rows.limits: No cue-induced script reflow; quoted Say speech and preparation notes remain distinct.

rows.name: Head-relative pointing targets
rows.options: RC4: centres bisect each saved head-edge/prompter-edge gap, at a shared below-eye height; words render above fixed markers.
rows.limits: Local reference geometry, not live gesture detection. Actual camera, mirror and multi-screen placement require UAT.

rows.name: HUD controller visibility
rows.options: RC4: one optional action across pad, phone and mapped inputs; companion 0.2.1.6 adds a Display function with its own icon.
rows.limits: Capability-gated; no per-direction keys, recorder action or automatic profile replacement.

rows.name: Theme settings
rows.options: Reading > Theme and background contains four built-in palettes and named custom reading themes.
rows.limits: Soft cream has a configurable light backing; existing cream profiles retain their prior colours until changed.

rows.name: Colours and themes
rows.options: Independent script, heading, inline-direction, production-note and background colour pickers; per-item Use theme reset.
rows.limits: Palette changes preserve custom colours; Use theme restores inheritance. Colour is separate from opacity and brightness.

rows.name: Script view preview
rows.options: Dedicated right column with Paused/Reading examples; compact windows use a Preview dialog.
rows.limits: Example controls never start prompting, microphone capture or recording.

rows.name: Portable reading themes
rows.options: Save current appearance under a name; restore, import or export reading-theme JSON.
rows.limits: Stores typography and reading background only, excluding controllers, recordings, windows, scripts and credentials.

rows.name: Text and heading fonts
rows.options: Four complete text targets: Segoe UI, Atkinson Hyperlegible, OpenDyslexic and Verdana, with Follow script for non-script text.
rows.limits: Fonts are installed/bundled locally; preference is not an accessibility certification.

rows.name: Script text size
rows.options: Toolbar and settings adjustment, with remote and voice size actions.
rows.limits: Available reading area depends on window dimensions and margins.

rows.name: Heading size
rows.options: Heading scale independent of the body text.
rows.limits: Long headings can require rewording or a smaller scale.

rows.name: Inline direction appearance
rows.options: Independent font, size, colour, bold, italic and line spacing; Normal/Dimmed/Hidden visibility.
rows.limits: Visibility no longer changes size. Explicit spoken quotations retain script styling and tracking.

rows.name: Production note appearance
rows.options: Independent font, size, colour, bold, italic and line spacing for HTML production notes.
rows.limits: Notes remain silent, show paused and hide during delivery. Existing note size remains independent of heading containers.

rows.name: Script paragraph spacing
rows.options: RC9: 0–300% in five-point steps under Spoken script; previews live and persists in settings and reading themes.
rows.limits: 100% preserves the existing one-em gap; older themes default to 100%. Heading and production-note block margins retain existing rules.

rows.name: Independent line spacing
rows.options: Separate script, heading, inline-direction and production-note spacing from 100–250%.
rows.limits: Each percentage is relative to that text type’s font height; paragraph spacing is independent.

rows.name: Alignment and margins
rows.options: Left or centred text; side, top and bottom margin controls.
rows.limits: Extreme settings can reduce the usable reading area.

rows.name: Background and text visibility
rows.options: Editable backing colour, off-air/on-air opacity, text opacity and brightness.
rows.limits: The appearance preview does not change the content behind the prompter.

rows.name: Text edge
rows.options: None, outline or shadow to separate words from a busy background.
rows.limits: Preview against the intended slides, call or camera picture.

rows.name: Focus band
rows.options: Dim spoken text away from the reading line; adjustable strength. Production comments and inline directions keep their own appearance; included in the reading workflow.
rows.limits: Strength appears only while enabled and is retained when off. Margin fading still applies to comments. No text is removed from the script or edit pack.

rows.name: Reading marker and progress
rows.options: Reading-line position and marker, sentence highlight, progress and time-left display.
rows.limits: Display aids can be configured separately from the script content.

rows.name: Transparent content overlay
rows.options: Read over a video call, slides, camera/projector preview or other desktop content.
rows.limits: Sightline does not supply or embed the underlying call or presentation.

rows.name: Always on top
rows.options: Keep the prompter above ordinary application windows.
rows.limits: Operating-system window rules and other topmost windows can affect stacking.

rows.name: Windowed and fullscreen use
rows.options: Size and position the prompter, or use a fullscreen reading view. RC10 wraps toolbar groups on small windows, retaining minimise/maximise/fullscreen/close controls.
rows.limits: Multi-window arrangements need checking on the intended display.

rows.name: Horizontal and vertical mirror
rows.options: Separate mirror controls, including toolbar icons.
rows.limits: Set the flips appropriate to the physical teleprompter glass or monitor.

rows.name: Prompter monitor
rows.options: Explicit display selection opens full screen. A manual cross-screen drag restores a centred normal window at 75% of the destination work area; included in the reading workflow.
rows.limits: Windows drag handling clears eye-line mode and the pinned monitor choice. Same-display moves retain the chosen size. Requires a connected display.

rows.name: Eye-line strip
rows.options: Compact reading strip with configurable screen height and reading-line position.
rows.limits: Lens alignment is a manual setup task.

rows.name: Click-through
rows.options: Let pointer interaction reach content beneath the overlay.
rows.limits: Use the documented shortcut or remote control to regain interaction.

rows.name: Operator window
rows.options: Separate upright controls and script/session status while the reading window is mirrored.
rows.limits: A second monitor is useful but not required.

rows.name: Toolbar hiding
rows.options: Toolbar retreats when the pointer moves away; faster distance-based hiding is included in 1.2.0.
rows.limits: Keyboard focus keeps controls available while they are in use.

rows.name: Pointer visibility
rows.options: Mouse pointer stays visible when the toolbar hides.
rows.limits: Click-through remains an independent preference.

rows.name: Utility windows
rows.options: Separate Settings, help and command windows, with movable positioning.
rows.limits: Window stacking must still be checked in the user's chosen fullscreen arrangement.

rows.name: Capture protection
rows.options: Request that supported capture paths exclude Sightline utility/reading windows.
rows.limits: Platform, capture method and compositor determine the result; verify the actual recording.

rows.name: Capture override for testing
rows.options: Debug control allows capture of Sightline windows for demonstrations and diagnostics.
rows.limits: This intentionally removes protection; inspect every captured output before recording.

rows.name: Small-screen layout
rows.options: Expanding area list, fixed named sections and compact Area/Section selectors with Preview action; no automatic pagination. Getting started alone scrolls its guidance in the centre pane.
rows.limits: Native checks cover 560 × 500 content and larger frames. Physical display/zoom and fullscreen stacking still require acceptance checks.

rows.name: Floating head guide
rows.options: Separate transparent framing window above a camera/projector view and below the prompter.
rows.limits: The underlying camera picture comes from another application.

rows.name: Ideal and Actual outlines
rows.options: Distinct target framing and manually aligned actual framing.
rows.limits: Actual is a user-set reference, not a camera measurement.

rows.name: Eye-line anchoring
rows.options: Set centre and eye level before adjusting the shape around the eyes.
rows.limits: Manual alignment must be repeated if camera framing changes.

rows.name: Head-edge adjustment
rows.options: Adjust top, bottom, left and right independently.
rows.limits: Changes the outline, not the camera crop or the person's image.

rows.name: Move and scale
rows.options: Horizontal/vertical position, overall size, width and height controls.
rows.limits: Shape adjustments are separate from moving the guide window itself.

rows.name: Guide visibility
rows.options: Stateful Show/Hide; bottom toolbar with hover-recoverable Head guide tab, Pin controls, lock/unlock, fullscreen, Move guide, Adjust and Guide off. Colour, opacity and Show Ideal remain in guide settings.
rows.limits: Small toolbar surface stays above the prompter while the outline retains its bounds. Guide off removes the controls and releases a hidden picture feed. Appearance and eye lock use Apply.

rows.name: Session framing reference
rows.options: Keep the guide pose, appearance and saved Ideal across scripts. Preparation and Ctrl+Shift+H share draft adjustments, optional detection and the recording position.
rows.limits: Target stays fixed as the person moves. Guide window/projector placement is manual; no automatic window fitting is claimed.

rows.name: Guide placements
rows.options: Centred and beside-prompter saved placements, plus window positioning and sizing; accessible from Settings and adjustments.
rows.limits: Placement/fullscreen actions act immediately; beside prompter means alongside the reading area.

rows.name: Fullscreen and chromeless guide
rows.options: Toggle the guide into and out of fullscreen; lock the adjustment view when ready.
rows.limits: Test stacking with the OBS projector and prompter on the chosen monitor.

rows.name: Adjustment panel
rows.options: Movable controls; bottom placement avoids the main top toolbar by default; preview refinement.
rows.limits: Dense small-screen combinations still have the separate known toolbar issue.

rows.name: Save Ideal
rows.options: Save the preferred target outline for repeatable framing.
rows.limits: This is distinct from saving an Actual reference for a recording.

rows.name: Save and restore recording reference
rows.options: Save Actual position, dimensions and eye lock from Settings or adjustments; restore without overwriting Ideal.
rows.limits: Restoring the shape does not restore the physical camera, body or guide window.

rows.name: Guide export metadata
rows.options: Record Ideal/Actual information, recording reference and guide window geometry in the edit pack.
rows.limits: Metadata describes the configured guide, not proof that it was absent from the video.

rows.name: Keep guide out of output
rows.options: Capture protection and a camera-source recording workflow keep the guide on the operator's screen.
rows.limits: No universal automatic guarantee; verify the recorded file and chosen capture source.

rows.name: Local position feedback
rows.options: Bundled local face/eye detection, fixed target and red/amber/green feedback in preparation and Ctrl+Shift+H. Distance includes overall Size, Width and both side adjustments, with a live target-size percentage and consistent mirrored arrows.
rows.limits: One well-lit face; grey means unavailable. Apparent width is not physical distance. Same scene/crop and manually matched guide bounds are required. No identity or gaze correction.

rows.name: OBS calibration scene
rows.options: Choose an actual scene from the connected OBS instance and read its preview frames for local detection. No programme-scene switch or recording command.
rows.limits: OBS integration must be enabled and available; camera choices remain when disabled. Sampled, centred 16:9 preview; does not test the production recording encoder or lip sync.

rows.name: Temporary calibration feed
rows.options: Explicitly start an OBS virtual camera for calibration, stopping it afterwards only when Sightline started it.
rows.limits: An existing virtual-camera session is retained. Connection loss may require manual confirmation/cleanup in OBS. Does not reconfigure the output or recording route.

rows.name: Pre-record workflow
rows.options: Camera alignment, manual fallback, audio check, actual short test recording and reviewed reference save. Calibration in Guide adjustments starts its shared service invisibly; only the explicit Prepare to record action opens the workflow. Inputs and retry remain available.
rows.limits: Explicit camera/microphone enable. Changing an input while capture is off keeps it off. A busy physical camera may require a virtual feed. Does not start OBS or production recording.

rows.name: Lock current framing
rows.options: Use detected eye centre and apparent size as a draft target while preserving custom guide proportions.
rows.limits: Does not replace the recording reference until the reviewed setup is explicitly saved. Out-of-range positions require guide adjustment before locking.

rows.name: Return after a break
rows.options: Restore the fixed target, match framing and recheck audio.
rows.limits: Same camera and resolution; original target/test retained. No silent recalibration.

rows.name: Local test recording
rows.options: Up to eight seconds of selected camera/microphone, actual WebM playback and picture/sound confirmation.
rows.limits: Local profile storage; manual review and hardware UAT required. No guide is burned into the camera clip.

rows.name: Persistent test outcomes
rows.options: Settings and the main prompter retain recording, review-required, passed, failed or check-again status.
rows.limits: Saving a clip alone is not a pass; the user must review picture and sound. A saved earlier pass is labelled as previous.

rows.name: Keyboard control
rows.options: Start/pause, sections, markers, display actions and documented shortcuts.
rows.limits: Some shortcuts depend on focused windows; documented global shortcuts cover specific actions.

rows.name: Presentation clickers
rows.options: Navigate using compatible keyboard-like presentation remotes.
rows.limits: Button codes vary by device and may need mapping.

rows.name: Pedals and gamepads
rows.options: Map supported input events to prompter actions.
rows.limits: Hardware, drivers and device-event support vary.

rows.name: Learn and customise input
rows.options: All keyboard/clicker and game-controller assignments appear in scrollable lists, with editable action and Remove on each row.
rows.limits: Driver/device support varies. No assignment is hidden solely by the selected row or window height.

rows.name: Editing input safeguards
rows.options: Reading-oriented mappings are suspended where editing requires ordinary input.
rows.limits: Check unusual remotes against the editor before live use.

rows.name: Common action model
rows.options: Navigation, display, take and framing actions are shared across applicable control surfaces.
rows.limits: Available buttons and feedback depend on the surface and enabled features.

rows.name: Floating control pad
rows.options: Separate touch/mouse window with configurable buttons. Settings shows the complete ordered list with drag, Earlier/Later and Remove.
rows.limits: Enable under Connections > Pad and phone. Longer lists scroll within Settings; presets replace the draft selection.

rows.name: Interface enable switches
rows.options: Speech, microphone, pad, phone, custom keys, game controller, Stream Deck, OBS and local API each have an enable switch.
rows.limits: Off hides configuration, preserves saved values and omits disabled actions/help. Dependencies remain a separate readiness check.

rows.name: Separate input mappings
rows.options: Keyboard/clickers and game controllers have distinct setup homes and enable switches.
rows.limits: Disabling custom mappings retains core shortcuts. Resetting one type preserves the other type.

rows.name: Select and reorder actions
rows.options: Choose the supported actions and drag to arrange their order.
rows.limits: The layout uses a defined action catalogue, not arbitrary third-party plugins.

rows.name: Pad column count
rows.options: Two, three, four or six columns.
rows.limits: Choose a count suitable for the available pad width.

rows.name: Layout presets
rows.options: Compact, Reading, Studio, and Framing & checks presets.
rows.limits: Applying a preset replaces the current selected layout.

rows.name: Reading buttons
rows.options: Start/pause, top, previous/next, pace, text and other supported reading actions.
rows.limits: State and button availability reflect the current session.

rows.name: Production buttons
rows.options: Marker, keeper, scrap, sound check and recorder controls.
rows.limits: OBS actions need OBS permission; other actions follow their own microphone/session requirements.

rows.name: Framing and listening buttons
rows.options: Guide visibility, fullscreen, available framing adjustments and listening controls.
rows.limits: No dial hardware is required to use equivalent button actions.

rows.name: Phone browser remote
rows.options: Open the supplied local-network URL or scan the QR code.
rows.limits: Phone and computer need network reachability; this is a browser controller, not a native phone app.

rows.name: Shared phone/pad layout
rows.options: Phone uses the same selected actions and order as the desktop pad.
rows.limits: Change the shared configuration in Sightline.

rows.name: Portrait and landscape
rows.options: Responsive button layout for phone orientation and screen size.
rows.limits: Long layouts can need scrolling; browser chrome reduces the usable height.

rows.name: Live state and reconnect
rows.options: Prompting, section/progress and confirmed recorder status; connection recovery feedback.
rows.limits: A disconnected client cannot confirm current state; network delays can affect response.

rows.name: Finish recording safeguard
rows.options: Hold Finish recording for one second on pad and phone.
rows.limits: This safeguard applies to those surfaces, not every external control route.

rows.name: Remote access security
rows.options: Token-based local-network access rather than an open public control page.
rows.limits: Treat a pairing URL/token as a control credential; this is not an internet relay service.

references.name: Stream Deck installation, permissions and profiles

rows.name: Companion plugin
rows.options: RC2 preview companion 0.2.1.1, paired with the app's supported control contract; stable companion remains 0.2.0.
rows.limits: Requires Elgato Stream Deck software; the companion is an optional installation.

rows.name: Grouped controller functions
rows.options: RC2 preview: related new assignments use a Function selector and function-specific key artwork; all 34 published key/dial UUIDs remain registered.
rows.limits: No compulsory conversion or automatic profile switch; legacy settings, states and custom images retain their rules.

rows.name: Controller preparation workflow
rows.options: RC2 preview: Prepare, combined room/voice check, test start/stop/play, detected draft lock, recording-reference restore/save and return after a break.
rows.limits: Explicit input enablement and existing framing/audio/test acceptance still apply; no automatic pass. Available from Stream Deck and shared pad/phone/mapped inputs.

rows.name: Explicit controller reading modes
rows.options: RC2 preview: Notes, Voice or Scroll; cycle skips disabled voice interfaces. Again reuses the current-section retake operation.
rows.limits: Pause before changing mode; script-forced Notes is respected. Existing two-mode keys retain their original behaviour.

rows.name: Configurable Adjustment dial
rows.options: RC2 preview: pace, text size, manual scroll, sections or backing, with visible press/tap behaviour.
rows.limits: Existing six dial UUIDs retain behaviour. New Sections turns move once per event; pace/size repeat up to five steps. Requires a dial-capable device.

rows.name: Workflow status and review keys
rows.options: RC2 preview: recorder/framing/preparation display, optional press, open current logged review and export a reviewed edit pack.
rows.limits: New displays default to no press. Export requires matching analysis and destination selection; no automatic transcription/model download.

rows.name: Virtual RC profiles
rows.options: RC2 preview: separate on-screen Virtual 8 × 5 and Plus layouts; existing standard/OBS profiles remain available.
rows.limits: Import explicitly. Virtual device type 11 is separate from MCP Deck type 14.

rows.name: Explicit recorder utilities
rows.options: RC2 preview: separate OBS pause and resume functions with confirmed-state feedback.
rows.limits: OBS enabled, connected and recording controls permitted; ordinary prompting pause retains its configured behaviour.

rows.name: Supported desktop hosts
rows.options: Plugin host support for Windows and macOS.
rows.limits: The Linux app does not imply an official Elgato Linux host.

rows.name: Keys, Mobile and Pedal
rows.options: Ready-made profiles for supported Stream Deck models, including Mobile and Pedal.
rows.limits: Requires the corresponding Elgato hardware/software entitlement where applicable.

rows.name: Stream Deck + dials
rows.options: Dial-based controls for supported reading and framing adjustments.
rows.limits: Requires Stream Deck + and the appropriate action configuration.

rows.name: Prompting and slots
rows.options: Play/pause, navigation, script slots, speed and display actions.
rows.limits: The companion controls loaded scripts; its restricted key does not grant script-file access.

rows.name: Take and recording keys
rows.options: Record take and Finish recording, markers and take ratings.
rows.limits: OBS recording keys require app integration plus explicit recording-control permission.

rows.name: Head-guide controls
rows.options: Show/hide, fullscreen and supported position/size/reference actions.
rows.limits: Adjusts the manual guide rather than a camera source.

rows.name: Session listening controls
rows.options: Supported command-listening actions from assigned keys.
rows.limits: Microphone permissions and selected engine remain app responsibilities.

rows.name: State on the keys
rows.options: Play/pause, On air, selected slot, section/time and confirmed recording state.
rows.limits: Unknown/disconnected recording state must not be treated as stopped.

rows.name: Recording profiles
rows.options: Separate OBS recording layouts alongside ordinary prompting profiles.
rows.limits: The Pedal recording layout's last pedal finishes the whole recording file.

rows.name: Discovery and pairing
rows.options: Enable once under Controls > Stream Deck; local discovery avoids manual token entry.
rows.limits: Preview pairing is separate from the normal installed app's discovery.

rows.name: Permission separation
rows.options: Dedicated restricted companion credential, separate from general AI/API access.
rows.limits: No arbitrary settings, recording-file access or broad AI permission is granted.

rows.name: Version compatibility
rows.options: App/plugin version reporting and required-feature compatibility feedback.
rows.limits: Use a matched app/plugin pair; successful installation is not hardware validation.

rows.name: Distribution and source
rows.options: [Published on Elgato Marketplace](https://marketplace.elgato.com/product/sightline-prompter-34676f28-e2e5-422d-9b48-e03dfd80bebe) as version 0.2; direct 0.2.0 installer also available with the app release. Source repository remains private.
rows.limits: Publication verified 9 November 2026. The 0.2.1 candidate is separate and not published; device, app and permission requirements still apply.

rows.name: Standalone OBS connection
rows.options: Connect through OBS WebSocket with address, port and password.
rows.limits: Requires OBS with a compatible WebSocket server, enabled and reachable.

rows.name: OBS connection test feedback
rows.options: Separate connection and recorder status; retained running/pass/fail test result in Settings and on the prompter.
rows.limits: Apply connection changes before testing. A connection pass is not a picture/sound recording pass.

rows.name: Optional integration
rows.options: OBS support is off until enabled; dependent help and controls follow that state.
rows.limits: Ordinary prompting works without OBS.

rows.name: Credentials
rows.options: Save the OBS password using supported operating-system protection; remove it from settings.
rows.limits: Operating-system credential protection availability and user profile apply.

rows.name: Status versus control permission
rows.options: Observe recorder state separately from permission to start, stop, pause and resume.
rows.limits: Connecting alone does not authorise recorder commands.

rows.name: Confirmed recording pill
rows.options: OFF green, RECORDING red, PAUSED orange and UNKNOWN grey; persistent included in 1.2.0.
rows.limits: Text accompanies colour; OBS-disabled mode hides it.

rows.name: Record take
rows.options: Confirm OBS recording before starting the prompter. RC8 voice aliases: record, start recording and begin.
rows.limits: Needs a healthy connection and recording-control permission. Gold command feedback also appears in Settings.

rows.name: Finish recording
rows.options: Finish the prompter session and request the end of the OBS recording.
rows.limits: Verify the acknowledged state and resolved file before handover.

rows.name: Continuous recording
rows.options: Keep one OBS recording running through prompting holds, section stops and retakes.
rows.limits: Default behaviour; a prompter pause is not an OBS pause.

rows.name: Linked recording
rows.options: Link recording to prompting: confirmed start/resume, pauses with holds, finish at final stop/end.
rows.limits: Enable with OBS stopped; requires recording permission and a pause-capable format. RC8 voice practice/go bypasses coupling, recorder directives, recorded slates and chapters without changing the saved preference.

rows.name: Explicit recorder actions
rows.options: Record on, off, pause and resume through supported controls, voice or optional directives.
rows.limits: OBS/format limitations apply; script loading alone cannot trigger recording.

rows.name: Recording reminder
rows.options: Visible recording state and start/finish controls help distinguish prompting from recording.
rows.limits: A reminder or On air display is not proof of a running recorder.

rows.name: Recording file and clock
rows.options: Log OBS recording starts/stops, pause/resume/restart events, file identity and reported time references.
rows.limits: File names and offsets remain unknown where OBS has not supplied enough information.

rows.name: Take-to-file references
rows.options: Section starts, takes and markers link to OBS recording segments and clock positions.
rows.limits: Estimated timing and discontinuities are retained as such; inspect the media for precise edits.

rows.name: OBS chapters
rows.options: Send section starts and named markers as recording chapters.
rows.limits: Requires support from the OBS version, output format and recording state.

rows.name: Recorded slate source
rows.options: Prepare a browser-source picture/tone route for a reference in the recorded output.
rows.limits: Add it to the recorded scene and include the routed audio track; confirm it in a test file.

rows.name: Setup assistant
rows.options: Review and apply a separate OBS profile/scene collection using selected existing camera, mic and presentation sources.
rows.limits: Does not guess hardware; source types must be supported and configured first.

rows.name: Output presets
rows.options: Choose a 1080p or 3840 × 2160 4K canvas/output at 30 fps and an output folder.
rows.limits: A 4K canvas does not prove native 4K capture or adequate encoding performance.

rows.name: Generated scene layout
rows.options: Camera and presentation layouts with selected microphone routed to tracks 1 and 2.
rows.limits: No head-guide/prompter capture source is added; track 2 in MKV is not a separate WAV.

rows.name: Preserve existing OBS setup
rows.options: Review named changes, use a separate profile/collection and check setup results.
rows.limits: Restoration and recording quality must still be verified on the actual workstation.

rows.name: Simultaneous clean-camera master
rows.options: Documented separate camera/microphone route using the Source Record filter.
rows.limits: Requires an additional OBS plugin and configuration; separate filenames are not discovered automatically.

rows.name: Unprocessed mic master
rows.options: Preserve the mic before processing using the documented separate route; extract PCM to WAV as appropriate.
rows.limits: A composed OBS track or Sightline scratch WAV is not automatically an unprocessed production master.

rows.name: Microphone level display
rows.options: Live sound-level information during applicable microphone use.
rows.limits: Measures the input as Sightline receives it, before another tool's later processing.

rows.name: Room and voice checks
rows.options: Separate background-noise and speech checks; the prompter meter appears automatically during measurement.
rows.limits: Previous meter visibility returns afterwards. Preparation relays existing measurements without opening a second microphone stream.

rows.name: Advisory low-level handling
rows.options: Explain quiet/noisy/clipping conditions and allow Continue anyway.
rows.limits: Increasing gain can also increase background noise; the user decides the compromise.

rows.name: Per-take loudness
rows.options: Voice-mode-only, Always during prompting, or Off.
rows.limits: Always mode opens the microphone during prompting; monitoring is not a mastering process.

rows.name: Logged audio measures
rows.options: Loudness LUFS, peak dBFS, background noise, voice-above-noise and warnings.
rows.limits: Available only when measured; accepted warnings are retained with the session.

rows.name: Scratch recording
rows.options: Independent local microphone WAVs for timing and edit checks.
rows.limits: Scratch audio is a reference, not a guarantee of production quality or a replacement for the clean mic master.

rows.name: Local take slate
rows.options: Off, Flash and beep, or Flash only; visible choices.
rows.limits: A flash seen only on the operator display does not prove recorded camera/audio sync.

rows.name: Recorded sync reference
rows.options: Slate IDs and known picture/tone routing into OBS, logged against takes.
rows.limits: The selected recorded scene and audio track must actually contain the reference.

rows.name: Physical camera lip sync
rows.options: Use visible/audible claps and inspect camera/mic recordings; compare later references for drift.
rows.limits: No automatic verified camera latency estimate or universal sync correction is claimed.

rows.name: Sync adjustment
rows.options: Apply verified offsets in OBS or in the external edit workflow.
rows.limits: Sightline metadata is a timing aid; validate the result by looking and listening.

rows.name: Measured file offsets
rows.options: RC1 preview: compare three audio windows for each master/clean-camera file; record method, scores, drift, source hashes and a session offset.
rows.limits: Optional local Python runtime. Ambiguous matches remain uncertain; audio alignment does not establish picture sync.

rows.name: Recorder-start sync reminder
rows.options: RC1 preview: remind after confirmed recording when a recorded slate route is unavailable.
rows.limits: No automatic clap verification or picture-sync pass. Prompter and recorder state remain separate.

rows.name: Session and section log
rows.options: Section/take IDs, start/end times, durations, UTC times and completion state.
rows.limits: Keep the recording media alongside the matching session export.

rows.name: Retakes and restarts
rows.options: Record reruns, section restarts, skipped or stopped takes and edit markers.
rows.limits: A logged restart is not automatically the point an editor should cut.

rows.name: Keeper and scrap choices
rows.options: Rate takes and preserve a preferred-use choice per section.
rows.limits: Choices are reviewable metadata, not destructive edits to media.

rows.name: Take summary
rows.options: Review pace, target difference, completion and available sound/recognition feedback.
rows.limits: Results depend on the information captured for that take.

rows.name: Saved recording browser
rows.options: Revisit saved sessions and export reports/edit packs.
rows.limits: The log browser is not a video editor or media-management system.

rows.name: Core log exports
rows.options: `take-log.json` and `takes.csv`.
rows.limits: Field availability can differ between older and newer sessions.

rows.name: Timing qualifications
rows.options: `timing-quality.json` and `TIMING-NOTES.md` explain unverified alignment, caption and pace estimates.
rows.limits: Original production brief and existing schemas are retained. Clock observations do not verify camera lip sync.

rows.name: Word and sentence detail
rows.options: `words.csv` and `sentences.csv` retain live voice-following estimates.
rows.limits: Word times can lag or bunch; unmatched words do not prove an omission. Use recorded-audio transcription for cuts and captions.

rows.name: Edit marks
rows.options: `edit-marks.csv` and `edit-marks.json`, including markers, pauses and rereads where available.
rows.limits: Suggestions and recognition-derived boundaries need editorial review.

rows.name: Draft captions
rows.options: `captions.srt` and `captions.vtt`, built from available aligned speech/script data.
rows.limits: Review text and timing before publication; not a guaranteed verbatim transcript.

rows.name: Script snapshot files
rows.options: `script-snapshots.json` plus numbered source snapshots tie words, IDs and cues to the recording.
rows.limits: Later edits to the source file do not replace the captured version.

rows.name: Production cue files
rows.options: RC3 preview: `production-cues.json`, CSV and human instructions retain authored cues plus per-take occurrences and keeper selection, with nearby spoken anchors.
rows.limits: Only exported for captured structured cues. Reviewed transcript anchors take priority; live estimates require review, unavailable time is null. Timing does not prove a gesture.

rows.name: Recorded sync export
rows.options: `recorded-sync.json` preserves reference IDs, routing and take/recording links.
rows.limits: Reference metadata does not certify the physical camera/microphone path.

rows.name: Head-guide export
rows.options: `head-guide.json` includes Ideal, Actual, saved reference and window geometry.
rows.limits: Reference save/restore is included in 1.2.0.

rows.name: Rehearsal export
rows.options: `rehearsal-coach.json` provides the available coaching report.
rows.limits: No performance score or automatic keeper reassignment is produced.

rows.name: Scratch WAV handover
rows.options: Include available independent mic recordings with their session/timing references.
rows.limits: Audio exists only when scratch capture was enabled and succeeded.

rows.name: External recording collection
rows.options: Main OBS filename is resolved when reported; collect video, clean camera and clean mic masters separately.
rows.limits: The edit pack does not automatically locate or bundle every external recording file.

rows.name: Automatic finished video
rows.options: Logs and edit packs support a human or an external editing agent.
rows.limits: Sightline does not render a finished promotional film or automatically edit the production master.

rows.name: Local post-record transcript
rows.options: RC1 preview: explicitly transcribe the selected reference audio with local faster-whisper small.en; progress, cancellation and recording guard.
rows.limits: Separate Python environment and cached English model; about 500 MB model download. No automatic post-stop job or cloud upload.

rows.name: Timed transcript import
rows.options: RC1 preview: import word/start/end or w/s/e JSON; choose session clock or provide a file offset.
rows.limits: Ordered finite word times required. No Python needed; an imported transcript still needs review.

rows.name: Recorded delivery comparison
rows.options: RC1 preview: expected/heard substitutions, insertions and omission candidates, with single-take priority and listening links.
rows.limits: Low agreement is uncertain, not a confirmed misread. Original take choices remain unchanged.

rows.name: Command cut ranges
rows.options: RC1 preview: post-record start/end ranges for recognised or missed attempts, with available live callback outcomes.
rows.limits: Review before cutting quoted commands. Legacy execution may be unknown; live callback times remain estimates and raw speech tracing stays opt-in.

rows.name: Script review
rows.options: Local review of script structure, reading load and supported directions before recording.
rows.limits: Rule-based feedback; no external generative AI is required.

rows.name: Directive checking
rows.options: Check known directives and values, including sample scripts and AI-generated drafts.
rows.limits: A syntactically valid script still needs a delivery rehearsal.

rows.name: Non-destructive suggestions
rows.options: Inspect findings and make deliberate edits in the script editor.
rows.limits: Review does not silently rewrite the script.

rows.name: Rehearsal pace
rows.options: Compare speaking pace, overall pace and section target times for finished takes.
rows.limits: Speaking and overall WPM include pauses differently.

rows.name: Coverage and rereads
rows.options: View matched, partly matched, not matched and outside-range text, plus logged rereads.
rows.limits: These are aligner findings, not confirmed mistakes; steady takes can lack alignment.

rows.name: Filler/repetition feedback
rows.options: Count recognised um, uh, erm, er and adjacent repeated-word candidates.
rows.limits: Explicit opt-in; recognition can omit fillers or count intentional/scripted repetition.

rows.name: Coaching data minimisation
rows.options: Filler feedback saves aggregate counts without starting an extra listener.
rows.limits: The selected engine's local/online processing still applies.

rows.name: Current and saved reports
rows.options: Open rehearsal reports from the current take summary or an earlier recording.
rows.limits: Reports identify the session; unavailable measurements are not invented.

rows.name: Performance grading
rows.options: Feedback assists the speaker's own judgement.
rows.limits: No emotion, confidence, acting-quality or universal delivery score is claimed.

references.name: Working with AI and the local API

rows.name: AI-optional workflow
rows.options: Write and run scripts yourself or work with a preferred external AI assistant.
rows.limits: No built-in cloud AI account is required for ordinary prompting.

rows.name: AI script brief
rows.options: Copy documented instructions for sections, targets, cues, stops and optional control directives.
rows.limits: The chosen assistant generates the script; check its output before use.

rows.name: Assistant choice
rows.options: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot or another assistant can prepare a compatible script.
rows.limits: Assistant capabilities, costs and privacy terms are external.

rows.name: Local control API
rows.options: Enable token-protected local endpoints to load scripts, select slots and issue supported commands.
rows.limits: Off by default; intended for authorised local tools, not public web pages.

rows.name: Local MCP connection
rows.options: Seven stdio tools in the AI kit; Connections > MCP, AI, and API includes a Configure MCP guide beside the switch.
rows.limits: Node.js 22.16+, local API/MCP enabled and applied. Separate grants; read-only by default. No cloud MCP endpoint. See [client configuration](guide/17-configure-mcp.md).

rows.name: MCP permission grants
rows.options: Script, prompting and OBS recording grants are enforced by the app; turning MCP off revokes active clients.
rows.limits: No settings edits, arbitrary file reads or recording deletion. Prompting requires the recording grant whenever OBS controls are enabled.

rows.name: Live automation feedback
rows.options: Status and event updates expose supported state and app/control-contract versions.
rows.limits: Clients need to handle connection loss, permissions and unsupported capabilities.

rows.name: Configure through an agent
rows.options: An authorised local agent can change supported settings and control prompting.
rows.limits: General API access is separate from the restricted Stream Deck credential.

rows.name: Recording-data access
rows.options: Authorised tools can retrieve saved-session and edit-pack information for editorial work.
rows.limits: Data access is not equivalent to an integrated video-editing engine.

rows.name: Agent kit
rows.options: Install the local command-line/helper kit and use its documented commands and reports.
rows.limits: Node.js is for the optional kit; packaged Sightline does not require a separate user Node installation.

rows.name: Dependency checks
rows.options: Show whether required local components are available before offering dependent operations.
rows.limits: A detected runtime does not establish that an AI agent has been configured or authorised.

rows.name: External AI edit assistance
rows.options: An editing agent can interpret takes, keeper choices, markers and timing exports.
rows.limits: Selecting or rendering a final edit depends on that external tool and human review.

rows.name: Built-in generative AI/video editor
rows.options: Sightline provides prompting, control and structured handover.
rows.limits: Script generation, synthetic narration and video rendering are external services/tools.

rows.name: Grouped settings
rows.options: Top-level task groups and focused subtabs separate prompting, appearance, recording and controls.
rows.limits: The detailed settings guide describes the current placement of each tool.

rows.name: Stable settings panel
rows.options: Eight task areas; 32 navigation homes with two additional OBS subviews. Controls and Components merge into Connections.
rows.limits: Approved navigation/control/sample composition is retained. Longer setup/result panels scroll centrally above a fixed footer; settings never migrate on resize.

rows.name: Settings example preview
rows.options: Inline example when width permits; movable non-modal companion on narrow windows. Both follow the same draft.
rows.limits: Settings remains usable while the companion is open. Examples never start prompting, a microphone or a recorder; the guide diagram is manual.

rows.name: Settings draft consistency
rows.options: Appearance previews; Apply persists, Save and close persists/closes, Cancel restores the last applied look.
rows.limits: Component installation, theme-library save/import, pairing reset, device tests and guide visibility/placement/reference saves are explicit actions.

rows.name: Numeric controls
rows.options: Slider/number pairs share whole-number or five-point increments; fine readouts have at most two decimals; included in the reading workflow.
rows.limits: Display rounding preserves stored precision until the control is adjusted.

rows.name: Named section navigation
rows.options: Sidebar search and visible button subtabs for Text, Screens, Reading aids, Head guide, add-ons and the single OBS entry.
rows.limits: OBS Connection, Recording control and Profile and scenes share one sidebar home. Disabled OBS/speech subviews remain unavailable.

rows.name: Live Tools groups
rows.options: Prepare, Adjust and During take share saved values with Settings through separate controls.
rows.limits: Live changes are immediate; a short prompter uses a utility window instead of clipping the menu.

rows.name: Contextual explanations
rows.options: Small question-mark pills beside options explain purpose and consequences on hover, keyboard focus or click. Both Reading aids groups have explanations for every control.
rows.limits: Escape closes the explanation. Help follows the selected mode and enabled components.

rows.name: Apply, save and cancel
rows.options: Review changed settings, apply them and keep or cancel the dialog changes.
rows.limits: Some setup operations and permissions have their own explicit controls.

rows.name: Onboarding and components
rows.options: First-use setup plus Getting started at the top of Settings, showing the current script, mode, text appearance and optional-tool guidance; included in the reading workflow.
rows.limits: Components remain optional. Opening guidance does not enable devices or integrations; changes use Apply.

rows.name: Restore defaults
rows.options: Getting started > Restore defaults returns preferences to the initial setup after confirmation.
rows.limits: Does not uninstall add-ons or delete scripts and recording media.

rows.name: Settings transfer
rows.options: Import/export supported settings in JSON or XML, including structured pad layouts and word lists.
rows.limits: Secrets and sensitive opt-ins are not a way to bypass explicit permissions.

rows.name: Settings access
rows.options: Toolbar settings control and a Settings item in the hamburger menu.
rows.limits: The menu remains an accessible route when toolbar icons are less obvious.

rows.name: Grouped help
rows.options: Tabbed shortcuts and commands; relevant help follows enabled modes/features.
rows.limits: Disabled OBS features do not need to display unusable recording keys.

rows.name: Built-in user guide
rows.options: Illustrated guide, settings screenshots, samples and recording acceptance walkthrough.
rows.limits: The shared source guide is canonical; a separate GitHub wiki is not enabled.

rows.name: Credits and attribution
rows.options: Product credits and attribution grouped in About.
rows.limits: Third-party licence notices still accompany their relevant distributions.

rows.name: Accessibility support
rows.options: Keyboard access, readable fonts, contrast themes, contextual explanations and consistent panels.
rows.limits: Manual screen-reader/magnification checks remain; no full accessibility-conformance claim.

rows.name: Guided coach marks
rows.options: RC1 preview: first-use offer; rerun from Getting started or Help; Next/Back, Skip, Escape and Finish; skip disabled integrations.
rows.limits: Navigation only: no Apply, device activation or model download. Pause prompting and finish recording before the tour.

rows.name: Local-first operation
rows.options: Scripts, settings and logs are held locally; local speech avoids a cloud recogniser.
rows.limits: Deepgram, document links and chosen external AI tools have their own network behaviour.

rows.name: No required telemetry account
rows.options: No Sightline sign-in is required to prompt or create local take logs.
rows.limits: Elgato, online recognition and AI providers can have independent accounts/telemetry.

rows.name: Local recording information
rows.options: Keep script snapshots, recognised timing, take choices and optional scratch audio for handover.
rows.limits: These files can contain personal or confidential content; manage them as production material.

rows.name: Diagnostic logging
rows.options: Debug > Status and recovery shows listening health, Restart listening and a speech-settings link. Recovery events help investigate failures.
rows.limits: Uses applied speech/microphone settings. Recognised-word tracing is separate and off by default.

rows.name: Optional word tracing
rows.options: Enable recognised command-word logging to investigate actual mishearings.
rows.limits: May include nearby speech; only enable it for the intended diagnostic period.

rows.name: Recording-state honesty
rows.options: Confirmed stopped/recording/paused states are distinct from unknown/disconnected.
rows.limits: UI state cannot certify that the resulting picture/audio is usable.

rows.name: Hardware acceptance
rows.options: Walkthrough covers real camera, mic, controls, clean tracks, sync and output inspection.
rows.limits: Local automated tests do not replace camera/mic and physical-control testing.

rows.name: Release and reference basis
rows.options: This grid describes Sightline 1.2.0 and companion 0.2.0, with versioned source and downloadable references.
rows.limits: Platform/device acceptance and the listed feature limits still apply. Historical RC notes are archived separately.

rows.name: Reviewer comparison scope
rows.options: Compare prompting, control, scripting, production handover, privacy and setup effort separately.
rows.limits: No competitor feature, price, performance ranking or endorsement is asserted here.
